headline: Dollar General comps rose 2% and it raised EPS guidance, but its core shoppers are squeezed by gas prices and SNAP cuts.
guidance_note: FY26 EPS raised to $7.20-7.45 (from $7.10-7.35); same-store sales 2.2-2.7% unchanged.
key_messages: Same-store sales +2.0% (traffic +1.4%, ticket +0.5%); revenue slightly below consensus, EPS $2.00 beat.
Tax-refund lift largely offset by higher fuel prices and reductions in SNAP benefit payments.
Core customers reported cutting back on other spending, including food, because of rising gas prices; worse in rural areas.
Higher gas prices historically bring trade-in from higher-income customers, and DG says it is seeing it again; biggest gain from $100K+ households.
Gross margin +65 bps to 31.6% on higher markups and lower shrink, partly offset by markdowns and transportation costs.

consumer.income_split: Core low-income customer financially constrained; largest increase in customer penetration came from households earning over $100,000.
consumer.pricing: Adding more $1 private-label and $1 frozen items; fuel prices and SNAP cuts eating into budgets.
consumer.quote: Elevated gas prices have historically led to increased trade-in from higher-income customers, and we are seeing this again.

macro_read: Higher gasoline prices and reduced SNAP payments are pinching rural, lower-income households even as better-off shoppers trade down to dollar stores.
